inputs.xtext_rule_text:
FeatureInverting returns SysML::FeatureInverting :
	( 'inverting' Identification? )?
	'inverse' 
	( featureInverted = [SysML::Feature| QualifiedName] 
	| ownedRelatedElement += OwnedFeatureChain )
	'of' 
	( invertingFeature = [SysML::Feature | QualifiedName]
	| ownedRelatedElement += OwnedFeatureChain )
	RelationshipBody
;

notes: The clause's second chain alternative reads `ownedRelationship += OwnedFeatureChain { ownedRelatedElement += invertingFeature }`, which never assigns invertingFeature and uses ownedRelationship where its first alternative uses the invertingFeature pattern. That is an abstract-syntax defect in the assignments; the syntax, OwnedFeatureChain, is unaffected. Whether it is filed was not searched.
decision: KerML 8.2.4.3.6 states FeatureInverting = ( 'inverting' Identification? )? 'inverse' ( featureInverted = [QualifiedName] | featureInverted = OwnedFeatureChain ) 'of' ( invertingFeature = [QualifiedName] | ownedRelationship += OwnedFeatureChain ) RelationshipBody. The KerML Xtext is the same syntax. The clause writes `Identification?` inside the group here, unlike its siblings; it is kept as written. The rule is the clause as written.
